A yellow sticky note is attached to the top right corner of the laptop lid in all photos.
The note reads: 'HP ELITE BOOK 840 G8 Core i5 16gb/512gb'.
The laptop is placed on top of a stack of plastic-wrapped items, possibly other laptops or documents.
The background is a dark, textured wall.
The HP logo is visible and centered on the lid.
No screen, keyboard, or ports are visible in any photo.
No serial number, model label, or internal components are shown.

risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic HP laptop with unknown specs, which is significantly lower than a verified 840 G8 with 16GB/512GB.

risks.risk: The laptop may be non-functional or have hardware issues (e.g., dead battery, damaged screen, no OS).
risks.proof: A video showing the laptop turning on, booting into Windows 11 Pro, and displaying the desktop with system specs visible.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, which is a major devaluation.

risks.risk: The laptop may be stolen or have a blacklisted serial number.
risks.proof: A photo of the serial number label on the bottom of the laptop, and a verification check (which cannot be done remotely).
risks.if_unproven: Priced with a discount for potential legal risk, as buyers may avoid such items.

A video of the laptop turning on and booting into Windows 11 Pro, showing system specs.
A photo of the screen displaying the Windows About page or BIOS showing RAM, storage, and processor details.
response.reason: The model and specs are claimed on a sticky note, not visible on the device. Without proof of internal components, OS, or serial number, the item cannot be priced accurately. The risk of misrepresentation or non-functionality is high.
